title: Double Fertilization: How a Flower Makes a Seed

generated.pipeline: extract → Opus draft → Sonnet accuracy gate → Sonnet fixes

cards.front: In a seed of a typical flowering plant, which tissues carry chromosomes from the pollen parent?
cards.back: Only the embryo and the endosperm. The seed coat and the fruit wall are the mother's own tissue.
cards.quote: The father reaches only the embryo and the endosperm; the seed coat and the fruit wall are the mother's own tissue.

cards.front: In most flowering plants, chromosome sets written maternal + paternal are: embryo 1 + 1, endosperm {{c1::2 + 1}}, seed coat and fruit wall 2 + 0.
cards.quote: embryo 1 + 1, endosperm 2 + 1, seed coat and fruit wall 2 + 0

cards.front: Name the four whorls of a typical flower, from the outside in, and where they sit.
cards.back: Sepals (the calyx), petals (the corolla), stamens (male) and carpels (female), on the receptacle, the swollen tip of the flower stalk.
cards.quote: Typically the organs sit in four rings, or whorls, on the swollen tip of the flower stalk, the receptacle.
cards.section: The parts of a flower: four rings of organs

cards.front: What are the three parts of a carpel, and what does the ovary hold?
cards.back: Stigma (sticky tip), style (neck) and ovary (swollen base). The ovary holds one or more ovules. Pollen forms in the anther of a stamen.
cards.quote: A carpel has a sticky tip, the stigma, a neck, the style, and a swollen base, the ovary, which holds one or more ovules.
cards.section: The parts of a flower: four rings of organs

cards.front: In a flowering plant, which generation is the pollen grain and the embryo sac, and what is the plant that bears the flower?
cards.back: Pollen grain (male) and embryo sac (female) are the haploid, gamete-making gametophytes. The flowering plant is the diploid, spore-making sporophyte.
cards.quote: a diploid, spore-making sporophyte alternates with a haploid, gamete-making gametophyte
cards.section: Before the sperm: two tiny generations

cards.front: Trace a pollen grain from the anther: which divisions make it, and what does each resulting cell do?
cards.back: A diploid microspore mother cell divides by meiosis into four haploid microspores. Each divides by mitosis into a tube (vegetative) cell, which grows the tube, and a generative cell, which divides into two sperm.
cards.quote: A diploid microspore mother cell divides by meiosis (chromosomes and meiosis) into four haploid microspores
cards.section: Before the sperm: two tiny generations

cards.front: In most flowering plants, which cells of the embryo sac matter for fertilization, and why do they all carry the same maternal set?
cards.back: The egg, a large central cell with two polar nuclei, and two synergids. All are mitotic copies of the one haploid megaspore's set.
cards.quote: Nuclei that are all mitotic copies of the megaspore's one set: the egg, a large central cell with two polar nuclei, and two synergids
cards.section: Before the sperm: two tiny generations

cards.front: What are the integuments of an ovule, and what opening do they leave?
cards.back: One or two layers of the mother's own diploid tissue around the embryo sac. They leave a small opening, the micropyle.
cards.quote: Around the embryo sac lie one or two layers of the mother's own diploid tissue, the integuments, which leave a small opening, the micropyle.
cards.section: Before the sperm: two tiny generations

cards.front: In Arabidopsis the two polar nuclei fuse before the sperm arrive. Does this change the endosperm's count of 2 maternal + 1 paternal sets?
cards.back: No. The fused central cell still carries two maternal sets, so the endosperm is still 2 + 1.
cards.quote: In Arabidopsis the two polar nuclei fuse before the sperm arrive, but the central cell still carries two maternal sets.
cards.section: Before the sperm: two tiny generations

cards.front: In flowering plants, distinguish pollination from fertilization.
cards.back: Pollination: transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma. Fertilization: fusion of a sperm with a female cell inside the ovule, which may never follow pollination.
cards.quote: fertilization, the fusion of a sperm with a female cell inside the ovule, which may never follow
cards.section: Pollen meets pistil: one tube, two fertilizations

cards.front: Flowering-plant sperm have no flagella. How do they reach the egg?
cards.back: On a compatible stigma the tube cell grows a pollen tube down the style into the ovary. Guided by chemical signals from the synergids, it enters the ovule, usually through the micropyle, and releases two sperm.
cards.quote: carrying sperm that have no flagella, and usually enters the ovule through the micropyle
cards.section: Pollen meets pistil: one tube, two fertilizations

cards.front: In double fertilization, sperm plus egg gives the diploid zygote, and sperm plus {{c1::central cell}} starts the endosperm.
cards.back: The endosperm is triploid (3n) in Arabidopsis, maize and most flowering plants.
cards.quote: The film's two fusions are double fertilization
cards.section: Pollen meets pistil: one tube, two fertilizations

cards.front: A mutant pollen tube delivers only one sperm to an ovule, and it fuses with the egg. The central cell stays unfertilized. What forms, and what is missing?
cards.back: A zygote forms, but no endosperm starts to feed it.
cards.why: The two fusions have separate jobs: sperm plus egg makes the zygote and embryo; sperm plus central cell starts the endosperm, the food store.
cards.quote: the endosperm they start is triploid (3n) in Arabidopsis, maize and most flowering plants
cards.section: Pollen meets pistil: one tube, two fertilizations

cards.front: Maize has 2n = 20. Why does its endosperm have 30 chromosomes while its embryo has 20?
cards.back: n = 10. The embryo is egg + sperm, 1 + 1 sets = 20. The endosperm is a two-set central cell plus one sperm, 3 sets x 10 = 30.
cards.quote: Endosperm: 2 maternal sets + 1 paternal set = 3 sets × 10 = 30.
cards.section: Worked problem: the yellow ear

cards.front: A flowering plant with a standard embryo sac (central cell with two polar nuclei) has 2n = 24. How many chromosomes are in its central cell, endosperm and seed coat?
cards.back: n = 12. Central cell 2 x 12 = 24; endosperm 3 x 12 = 36; seed coat (mother's diploid tissue) 24.
cards.why: Multiply the number of sets by n. The seed coat is maternal tissue, not a gamete.
cards.quote: Multiply sets by n, the chromosomes in one set, to get chromosome numbers; follow alleles through the sets to get kernel colours.
cards.section: Worked problem: the yellow ear

cards.front: A white-kernelled maize plant (yy, one gene for endosperm colour, yellow dominant) is pollinated by a true-breeding yellow plant (YY). What colour are this season's kernels on the white plant, and which tissue sets it?
cards.back: Yellow. Egg y, central cell yy, sperm Y: the embryo is Yy and the endosperm yyY, so the endosperm's Y shows.
cards.why: The endosperm is a product of fertilization, so the pollen parent's genes show in this generation's seed (xenia).
cards.quote: Because the endosperm is a product of fertilization, the pollen parent's genes show in this generation's seed: xenia.
cards.section: Worked problem: the yellow ear

cards.front: A maize kernel colour is carried in the pericarp. A plant is pollinated by a plant of a different pericarp genotype. Does this season's pericarp colour change with the pollen parent?
cards.back: No. The pericarp is fruit wall fused to the seed coat, the mother's own tissue (2 + 0 sets), so the mother's genotype sets its colour.
cards.quote: A colour carried in the pericarp, the fruit wall around each kernel, is set by the mother's genotype
cards.section: Worked problem: the yellow ear

cards.front: In maize, where the yellow of the endosperm deepens with each extra Y copy, compare Yy female x yy male with yy female x Yy male. Half the kernels are yellow in both. Which cross gives the deeper yellow kernels?
cards.back: Yy female x yy male. Its yellow kernels have endosperm YYy (two doses); a Y from the father comes in one sperm, giving yyY (one dose).
cards.why: Both polar nuclei copy the egg's set, so a Yy mother's central cell is YY or yy, never Yy. The rule counts sets, not alleles.
cards.quote: A Yy mother's central cell is YY or yy, never Yy, so a yellow kernel's endosperm is YYy, two doses of Y.
cards.section: Worked problem: the yellow ear

cards.front: A Yy maize plant self-pollinates and an ear sets 400 kernels (yellow dominant, endosperm colour). How many yellow and white kernels do you expect?
cards.back: Endosperm YYY, YYy, yyY or yyy, each 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4. Only yyy is white: 1/4 x 400 = 100 white, 3/4 x 400 = 300 yellow.
cards.why: Assumes random fertilization and equal kernel survival.
cards.quote: so the endosperm is YYY, YYy, yyY or yyy, each 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4
cards.section: Selfing a heterozygote: counting kernels on an ear of 400

cards.front: A Yy maize plant self-pollinates; yellow deepens with each Y copy in the endosperm. What fraction of its yellow kernels have two or more doses of Y?
cards.back: 2/3. YYY and YYy are 1/4 each (1/2 of all kernels); all yellow kernels are 3/4; 1/2 / 3/4 = 2/3.
cards.why: Rests on two rules: the central cell copies the egg's set (YY or yy), and the sperm adds one independent set.
cards.quote: Both polar nuclei copy the egg's set, so the central cell is YY when the egg is Y and yy when it is y, each with probability 1/2.
cards.section: Selfing a heterozygote: counting kernels on an ear of 400

cards.front: Suppose a water lily (one polar nucleus) has 2n = 28. A yy mother is pollinated by a YY plant. Give the endosperm's sets, genotype and chromosome number.
cards.back: 1 maternal + 1 paternal set: genotype yY, 2 x 14 = 28 chromosomes, diploid endosperm.
cards.why: The logic is unchanged; one polar nucleus means one maternal set in the central cell instead of two.
cards.quote: Water lilies, with one polar nucleus, make diploid endosperm, 1 maternal + 1 paternal set.
cards.section: When the count changes

cards.front: What flower traits mark a wind-pollinated plant such as maize or oak, and why does it shed so much pollen?
cards.back: Small petals or none, no nectar, exposed stigmas, and huge amounts of light, dry pollen, because almost all of it lands nowhere useful.
cards.quote: shed huge amounts of light, dry pollen, almost all of which lands nowhere useful
cards.section: Flowers and their animals: wind, insects and coevolution

cards.front: How does an animal-pollinated flower such as field mustard (Brassica rapa) get its pollen to the next flower?
cards.back: Its petals, scent and nectar attract visitors such as bees and hoverflies, and its sticky pollen travels on them.
cards.quote: Its petals, scent and nectar attract visitors, and its sticky pollen travels on them to the next flower.
cards.section: Flowers and their animals: wind, insects and coevolution

cards.front: Why is self-pollination still sexual reproduction, and what follows for a heterozygous plant's selfed offspring?
cards.back: It uses meiosis and fertilization, so a heterozygous plant's selfed offspring vary.
cards.quote: Selfing is still sexual: it uses meiosis and fertilization, so a heterozygous plant's selfed offspring vary.
cards.section: Flowers and their animals: wind, insects and coevolution

cards.front: What is self-incompatibility in flowering plants?
cards.back: The stigma or style rejects pollen carrying the plant's own incompatibility alleles. Wild Brassica rapa has it.
cards.quote: the stigma or style rejects pollen carrying the plant's own incompatibility alleles
cards.section: Flowers and their animals: wind, insects and coevolution

cards.front: {{c1::Coevolution}} is reciprocal evolutionary change between interacting lineages: each changes in response to the other.
cards.quote: Coevolution is reciprocal evolutionary change between interacting lineages: each changes in response to the other
cards.section: Flowers and their animals: wind, insects and coevolution

cards.front: The orchid Angraecum sesquipedale hides nectar at the bottom of a spur nearly 30 cm long, and a hawkmoth has a tongue to match. Why is the match alone not evidence of coevolution?
cards.back: A match is a hypothesis. Coevolution needs selection on both sides: tongues selecting spur length and spurs selecting tongue length.
cards.why: If the tongue lengthened for other reasons and the orchid tracked it, that is one-sided adaptation.
cards.quote: A match like this suggests an interaction; on its own it is a hypothesis, not evidence of coevolution.
cards.section: Flowers and their animals: wind, insects and coevolution

cards.front: Fast-cycling Brassica rapa populations were pollinated only by bumblebees, only by hoverflies, or by hand, with three replicate populations per treatment, for nine generations in one greenhouse. What does the hand-pollinated treatment rule out, and what do the replicates test?
cards.back: Hand-pollinated lines rule out greenhouse effects for traits that changed only in insect lines. Replicates test repeatability: drift pushes replicates in different directions, selection by one pollinator pushes them the same way.
cards.quote: Three replicates test repeatability: drift would push replicates in different directions, while selection by one pollinator should push them the same way.
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: Brassica rapa lines pollinated only by hoverflies evolved to self-pollinate more. Give one hypothesis for why.
cards.back: Where a pollinator delivers little outcross pollen, plants that self may leave more offspring.
cards.quote: where a pollinator delivers little outcross pollen, plants that selfed may leave more offspring
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: After nine generations of bumblebee-only pollination, Brassica rapa plants grew taller and bumblebees preferred them. Does this show coevolution, and what more would you need?
cards.back: No. It shows pollinators can drive plant evolution quickly. Only the plants were followed, so you would also need insects whose traits changed in response to the plants.
cards.why: Coevolution requires reciprocal change. One pollinator in a greenhouse also shows what pollinators can do, not what they do in a meadow.
cards.quote: only the plants were followed, so you would also need insects whose traits changed in response to the plants
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: After double fertilization, what does each part become: zygote, fertilized central cell, integuments, ovary?
cards.back: Zygote: embryo (root tip, shoot tip, one or two cotyledons). Fertilized central cell: endosperm. Integuments: seed coat. Ovary: fruit, with its wall (in a maize grain, the pericarp).
cards.quote: The embryo is a new diploid plant with a root tip, a shoot tip and one or two seed leaves (cotyledons); the seed coat comes from the integuments.
cards.section: From ovule to seed, ovary to fruit

cards.front: A mature bean seed is cut open: there is almost no endosperm, but two thick cotyledons. Did double fertilization fail?
cards.back: No. In beans, peas and Capsella the cotyledons absorb the endosperm as the seed develops and store the food themselves. In maize and wheat the endosperm persists and holds the starch.
cards.quote: the cotyledons absorb it as the seed develops and store the food themselves
cards.section: From ovule to seed, ovary to fruit

cards.front: Pollinated strawberry receptacles stripped of their achenes do not grow; those left with one strip of achenes swell only beneath it; stripped ones coated with auxin paste grow. What do the results show?
cards.back: Developing achenes supply a local signal for receptacle growth, and applied auxin can mimic it.
cards.why: The red flesh is the mother's tissue, yet it grows only where achenes, the true fruits, develop.
cards.quote: A strawberry's red flesh is the mother's own tissue, yet it swells only after the flower is pollinated.
cards.section: From ovule to seed, ovary to fruit

cards.front: In Fragaria vesca, applied auxin enlarges the receptacle, but less so when a gibberellin-synthesis blocker is added. What does this suggest about strawberry growth signals?
cards.back: The blocker reduced auxin-induced enlargement, which points to gibberellins also being involved in strawberry growth. Auxin transport from achene to receptacle remains a proposed model.
cards.quote: a gibberellin-synthesis blocker reduced the enlargement caused by applied auxin
cards.section: Auxin and gibberellin in strawberry growth

cards.front: Seed dormancy is the failure of an intact, viable seed to complete {{c1::germination}} under favourable conditions.
cards.quote: Seed dormancy is the failure of an intact, viable seed to complete germination under favourable conditions.
cards.section: Waiting and travelling: dormancy, dispersal and clones

cards.front: In the framework used in Arabidopsis seed studies, what do abscisic acid and gibberellins do, and what marks the start and end of germination?
cards.back: ABA is required to induce dormancy as the seed matures; gibberellins promote germination. Germination begins with water uptake and ends when the embryonic root pushes out through the coverings.
cards.quote: the hormone abscisic acid (ABA) is required to induce dormancy as the seed matures
cards.section: Waiting and travelling: dormancy, dispersal and clones

cards.front: Freshly harvested Arabidopsis seeds sown under favourable conditions: about 70% of wild type and about 10% of the ahg1-5 mutant germinate in 7 days. Of 500 seeds of each, how many more wild-type seeds germinate, and which line is more dormant?
cards.quote: Seed dormancy is the failure of an intact, viable seed to complete germination under favourable conditions.
cards.section: Waiting and travelling: dormancy, dispersal and clones

cards.front: How are dandelion fruits, coconut fruits and acorns dispersed?
cards.back: Dandelion: a parachute of fine hairs on the wind. Coconut: floats by sea. Acorns: jays and squirrels bury them and miss some.
cards.quote: Jays and squirrels bury acorns and miss some, which germinate away from the parent oak.
cards.section: Waiting and travelling: dormancy, dispersal and clones

cards.front: What are strawberry stolons and potato tubers?
cards.back: Stolons (runners): horizontal stems that root at their nodes into new plants. Tubers: swollen underground stems whose buds (eyes) sprout.
cards.quote: Strawberry stolons, or runners, are horizontal stems that root at their nodes into new plants.
cards.section: Waiting and travelling: dormancy, dispersal and clones

cards.front: {{c1::Apomixis}} is seed formation in which the embryo develops without fertilization from an unreduced cell, one that keeps the mother's full chromosome number.
cards.back: Dandelions are a familiar example.
cards.quote: Apomixis is seed formation in which the embryo develops without fertilization from an unreduced cell, one that keeps the mother's full chromosome number.
cards.section: Waiting and travelling: dormancy, dispersal and clones

cards.front: A plant heterozygous at three unlinked genes (Aa Bb Cc) sets seed with no pollinators. What fraction of seedlings are Aa Bb Cc if the seeds came from selfing, and if they came from apomixis?
cards.back: Selfing: 1/2 x 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/8. Apomixis: all of them.
cards.why: An apomictic embryo carries all of the mother's sets and none from a father, a clone; selfed seedlings segregate.
cards.quote: All of the mother's sets (2 in a diploid mother) and none from a father: a clone, so every seedling keeps every heterozygous gene.
cards.section: Waiting and travelling: dormancy, dispersal and clones

cards.front: A high-yielding hybrid crop is heterozygous at many genes. Predict what happens to uniformity if its seed comes from selfing versus apomixis.
cards.back: Selfed seed segregates, so the next generation varies and loses the hybrid genotype. Apomictic seed is a clone that keeps every heterozygous gene, so the hybrid breeds true.
cards.why: Rests on: selfing uses meiosis and fertilization; apomixis skips both. In one engineered hybrid rice, apomixis was still inefficient.
cards.quote: Engineered apomixis is being studied to keep the best hybrid crops true, but in one hybrid rice it was still inefficient
cards.section: Waiting and travelling: dormancy, dispersal and clones

cards.front: A white (yy) maize ear is dusted with a mix of YY and yy pollen. Some kernels come out yellow. What pollen fertilized a yellow kernel, and what is that kernel's embryo genotype?
cards.back: A grain from the YY plant. Its endosperm is yyY, and its embryo is Yy, because both sperm of one tube carry the same paternal set.
cards.why: Endosperm is a product of fertilization (xenia), and each pollen tube brings one paternal set in each of its two sperm, made from one generative cell.
cards.quote: The pollen tube brings one paternal set in each of its two sperm.
